title: Grade 4 Math — Wed, Jun 18
description: Geometry — Day 3 of 5: Acute, obtuse, and reflex angles
subject: mathematics

questions.question: An acute angle is an angle that measures:
questions.explanation: An acute angle is less than 90°. Think 'cute and small'. Examples: 30°, 45°, 60°, 89°.

questions.question: An obtuse angle is an angle that measures:
questions.explanation: An obtuse angle is between 90° and 180°. It is wider than a right angle but less than a straight line.

questions.question: A reflex angle is an angle that measures:
questions.explanation: A reflex angle is greater than 180° but less than 360°. It goes more than halfway around.

questions.question: Classify 180°:
questions.explanation: Exactly 180° = straight angle. It looks like a straight line.

questions.question: The angle between the hour and minute hand at 2 o'clock is 60°. What type of angle is this?
The angle between the hour and minute hand at 9 o'clock is 90°. This is a:
questions.explanation: At 9 o'clock, the hands are at 90° = right angle.

questions.question: Which triangle has an obtuse angle?
questions.explanation: A triangle with 110° has one obtuse angle (> 90°). This is an obtuse triangle.

questions.question: Is it possible for a triangle to have two obtuse angles?
options: No — three angles must add up to 180°, and two obtuse angles would exceed 180°
Yes, if one angle is acute
questions.explanation: Two obtuse angles > 90° + 90° = 180°. Since all three angles of a triangle sum to 180°, you cannot have two obtuse angles.

questions.question: A pizza slice cut at 30° from the centre has what type of angle?
questions.explanation: 30° < 90° → acute angle. A narrow pizza slice has an acute angle at the tip.

questions.question: Order from smallest to largest: Right angle, Acute angle, Obtuse angle, Reflex angle:
questions.explanation: Acute (< 90°) → Right (= 90°) → Obtuse (90°–180°) → Reflex (180°–360°). This is the correct order.

questions.question: A reflex angle and its corresponding angle (the part not covered) together make:
questions.explanation: A reflex angle + its corresponding angle = 360° (a full rotation). For example, 270° reflex + 90° = 360°.
